jobs.title: Invasive Non-Native Species Scientist (Water Management Consultancy)
jobs.description:
Overview

Be part of the solution - shape the future of our water environment.

Do you have the drive, skills and career potential to work with us as an experienced invasive species scientist, influencing environmental outcomes for our freshwater systems at the project level and beyond? We are seeking to further expand our team of freshwater ecologists within AtkinsRéalis' Water Management Consultancy. If you are looking to join an established team focused on the delivery of interesting and significant projects, framed by a strong culture of wellbeing, innovation and inclusivity, this is the place for you.

Our Water Management Consultancy operates at the interface between people and the water environment. Our key services cover all aspects of water management including aquatic ecology, hydromorphology, river restoration, flood and coastal erosion risk management, integrated catchment management, regulation and assurance, strategic asset management, water resources and water quality planning, hydrogeology and hydrology, climate futures and resilience, coastal and marine environmental management, natural capital and Biodiversity Net Gain assessment and economic appraisal. We have a reputation for technical excellence, innovation and actively shaping the future of our industry. We are a friendly and approachable team. We enjoy the work we do and have fun while doing it.

We have a huge variety of projects on-the-go at any one time. So, when you start this role with us, it could take your career wherever your interests lie. You'll find everyone here is willing to pitch in and help because we all want you to succeed, and we're ready to help you grow.

When it comes to living your life, we want you to get the most out of it. So, talk to us about all our flexible and remote working policies that can support your personal priorities. Also, ask us about some of our recent pledges for Women's'Equality, as well as being a 'Disability Confident' and 'Inclusive Employer.'"

AtkinsRéalis is one of the world's most respected design, engineering and project management consultancies. Our global team of over 38,000 employees speaks over 70 languages and represents 130 nationalities across six continents. At AtkinsRéalis, we offer more than just a job. We offer an opportunity to make a difference and shape the world to benefit future generations and the natural environment.

We understand the need for a diverse and flexible workforce, where a work-life balance is important. So, by default AtkinsRéalis offers flexible working, where there is no fixed 9 'till 5, no need for a 5-day week, no requirement for a full-time contract, and no requirement to spend all your working time in the office. Our IT systems support homeworking, so where you have parental or carer duties; or you simply need to be elsewhere for a parcel, servicing your car, or waiting in for a tradesperson; AtkinsRéalis will work for you. Similarly, AtkinsRéalis' corporate social responsibility provides the opportunity to give something back to the community, and we run professional networks supporting groups such as local schools, charities, parents, those coming out of the armed-forces and women in engineering.

As an experienced aquatic ecologist with a focus on assessing and managing the impacts of invasive non-native species (INNS) on the freshwater environment, you can expect to support the delivery of work within our INNS Service Line team. Your work will produce tangible improvements within river catchments throughout the UK support by the dynamic and influential relationship between our aquatic ecology team, water resource specialists and our engineering design and planning colleagues. Our structure and growing project portfolio will provide exceptional opportunities for you to develop your career.

You should have a strong technical background in aquatic INNS investigation and management, that includes application of industry standard risk assessment tools (e.g., SAI-RAT) for water resource transfers, the development and management of INNS monitoring programmes and analysis of ecological monitoring data. You should exhibit strong collaborative behaviours to interface with other technical specialists.

You will also have the chance to develop yourself though wider opportunities and support on our increasing portfolio of UK water resource investigations, infrastructure planning and development support, and habitat management and design projects. We work for clients across the UK and overseas, including water companies, central government, regulators, NGOs and local authorities.

This Position is open for Birmingham, Bristol, Derby, Epsom, Glasgow, Edinburgh, Manchester, Oxford or Peterborough Offices.

Your role

To support water resource INNS investigations and develop the application of risk assessment tools for our key water company and regulatory clients.
To support our INNS Service Line team with work activities through integration and collaboration with multi-disciplinary teams and bring your technical knowledge and influence to bear in securing the best outcomes for the environment and our clients.
To support the development and application of emerging approaches in INNS management, transfer and control to ensure the technical development of staff within our aquatic ecology team.
To support large scale INNS/ aquatic species monitoring programmes through collaborative working with our internal teams and supply chain.
To support our national aquatic ecology team in leading ecological input to projects including field surveys and technical reporting, as well as assisting on the delivery of a wide range of catchment science projects with a focus on river and wetland function, habitat design, management and restoration, hydroecology, ecological impact assessment, Water Framework Directive compliance and Biodiversity Net Gain.
To drive and secure positive outcomes for the environment, delivering technical consultancy services across a huge range of AtkinsRéalis core markets and services.
To maintain excellent relationships with other professionals (environmental scientists, engineers, planning consultants) throughout AtkinsRéalis to provide a consistent and integrated service to clients.
To develop your technical skills through Continuing Professional Development.

About You

Experience of invasive non-native species with a specific focus on the assessment of aquatic INNS transfer risk, with knowledge of programme, resource and financial management.
A degree in a relevant discipline is essential and a post-graduate qualification desirable (with focus on invasive species/ hydroecology and/or catchment management), with consultancy experience.
Willing to work towards securing chartership, with support and mentorship from chartered colleagues within AtkinsRéalis.
In using and developing risk assessment approaches, the role requires someone highly numerate, literate and familiar with IT and software appropriate to the tasks undertaken.
Experience of working on large water resource projects as part of a multidisciplinary team is desirable, as is experience of specifying, undertaking and managing the delivery of invasive species surveys.
Highly motivated and proactive; focussed on achieving and delivering technical excellence.
Skilled at collaborative working, with good interpersonal skills and an ability to communicate effectively.
To succeed within this role, you must have a flexible, 'hands-on', proactive approach to your work. You must be able to work independently as well as part of a wider team and be comfortable applying your skills in a commercial environment.

Rewards & benefits

Explore the rewards and benefits that help you thrive – at every stage of your life and your career. Enjoy competitive salaries, employee rewards and a brilliant range of benefits you can tailor to suit your own health, wellbeing, financial and lifestyle choices. Make the most of a myriad of opportunities for training and professional development to grow your skills and expertise. And combine our hybrid working culture and flexible holiday allowances to balance a great job and fulfilling personal life.

Be rewarded. Find out more.

About AtkinsRéalis

We're AtkinsRéalis, a world-class engineering services and nuclear organization. We connect people, data and technology to transform the world's'infrastructure and energy systems. Together, with our industry partners and clients, and our global team of consultants, designers, engineers and project managers, we can change the world. We're committed to leading our clients across our various end markets to engineer a better future for our planet and its people.

Find out more.

Security clearance

This role may require security clearance and offers of employment will be dependent on obtaining the relevant level of clearance. If this is necessary, it will be discussed with you at interview. The vetting process is delivered by United Kingdom Security Vetting (UKSV) and may require candidates to provide proof of residency in the UK of 5 years or longer. If applying to this role please do not make reference to (in conversation) or include in your application or CV, details of any current or previously held security clearance.

As an Equal Opportunities Employer, we value applications from all backgrounds, cultures and ability. Job Summary

The Environmental Compliance Specialist III is responsible for ensuring applicable product registrations are properly applied for and approved by state and federal regulations. This position is also responsible for the timely submission of Tier II Chemical Inventory Reports and Hazardous Materials Business Plans for affected locations per federal, state, and local municipality requirements. In addition, this position is responsible for collecting and reporting ESG data streams for our facilities worldwide.

Responsibilities

Researches and documents regulatory changes affecting areas of responsibility.
Analyzes new proposed regulations to determine impact on company operations.
Collaborates with EPA Regulatory Affairs Manager to create and implement processes and
procedures to comply with new regulations in all areas of responsibility.
Collaborates with EPA Regulatory Affairs Manager to create regulatory compliance burden analysis
and report for Executive Team.
Researches and analyzes state and federal requirements for product registration guidelines to
conduct pesticide product registrations.
Collects and analyzes private label registration data to establish and maintain state restrictions in operational systems. (QC/QA)
Collects and analyzes chemical inventory reports from each sales center to properly submit required reporting by the established deadlines.
Maintains inventories of SDS (Safety Data Sheets) for all required products.
Maintains and updates chemical descriptions within company operating systems for required Department of Transportation (DOT) shipping paperwork.
Collects, analyzes, and prepares reports on ESG data streams for our locations worldwide.
Collaborates with ESG Reporting Committee to ensure deadlines for deliverables.
Summarizes ESG data, provides previous years comparison to Financial Reporting Team.
Effectively works with various company departments to ensure products are being properly established per company set protocol.
Performs Quality Control /Quality Assurance Audits in areas of responsibility.
Assists with day to day management of environmental contracts, sustainability projects and vendor compliance Quality Assurance initiatives.
Assists with various governmental agency inspections that are performed at company locations.
Other duties as assigned.

Requirements

Bachelor’s degree and 4 to 6 years of related practical experience working in government compliance (i.e. FDA, EPA, DOT, etc.); or equivalent combination of education and experience.
Ability to read and interpret documents such as safety rules, operating and maintenance instructions, and procedural manuals. Ability to write routine reports and correspondences.
Strong computer skills including proficiency in MS Office software, especially MS Excel.
Effective communication skills both verbal and written.
Experience with Tier II and CUPA Hazardous Materials Business Plan submittals preferred.

The Aerospace Corporation is the trusted partner to the nation’s space programs, solving the hardest problems and providing unmatched technical expertise. As the operator of a federally funded research and development center (FFRDC), we are broadly engaged across all aspects of space— delivering innovative solutions that span satellite, launch, ground, and cyber systems for defense, civil and commercial customers. When you join our team, you’ll be part of a special collection of problem solvers, thought leaders, and innovators. Join us and take your place in space.

The Defense Systems Group (DSG) provides analysis-based decision support to senior leaders on space architectures, policy and strategy, technology development, warfighter capability enablers, systems integration, defense industrial base, and threat reduction to help shape existing and future space missions across the National Security Space enterprise. DSG is unique at Aerospace as it not only directly supports major customers, including the U.S. Space Force (USSF), U.S. Space Command, Air Force Materiel Command, and senior leadership at the Pentagon, but also provides a broad range of technical support across the national space enterprise, maintaining vertical responsibilities within customers’ portfolios as well as horizontal, matrixed responsibilities across the corporation. In particular, DSG provides deep technical expertise to USSF acquisition organizations in the conception, design, acquisition, launch and operations of satellite, launch vehicle, ground control, and range systems.

The Space Environment and Weather Programs (SEWP) Department directly supports USSF System Delta 810 in providing mission assurance and technical acquisition expertise for all space environment and weather programs. The SEWP Department is in need of a Space Based Environmental Monitoring Systems Engineer
. The successful candidate will support current major programs, including the Weather System Follow-On - Microwave (WSF-M) and the Electro-Optical and Infrared (EO/IR) Weather System (EWS), as well as planned prototypes and future programs.

The selected candidate will be required to work full-time, on-site at our facility at Los Angeles Air Force Base located in El Segundo, CA.

What You’ll Be Doing

Provide technical support to USSF, System Delta 810
Ensure successful acquisition of WSF-M, EWS, and other programs
Perform independent risk assessments, manage the Aerospace internal risk framework, and ensure risk-informed decision making by both the customer and Aerospace leadership
Engage the customer and Aerospace leadership with impact:
Work cooperatively and respectfully with others across the organization to achieve shared objectives
Deliberately and proactively share and exchange knowledge and information
Communicate in a clear and concise manner

What You Need To Be Successful

Minimum Requirements for the Project Engineer – Systems Engineering:

Bachelors degree in engineering, physics, math or related STEM field
6 or more years of experience in Space Systems Engineering
Experience in verification and validation (V&V) of space and ground systems
Experience in risk management of space and ground acquisition programs
Excellent attention to detail, record keeping & organization skills, and communication skills
Willing to travel approximately 25% (as required)
Ability to obtain and maintain a security clearance, which is issued by the U.S. government. U.S. citizenship is required to obtain a security clearance.

In addition to the above, the minimum requirements for the Sr. Project Engineer – Systems Engineering include :

Bachelors degree in engineering, physics, math or related STEM field
12 or more years of experience in space and ground systems engineering
Experience with assembly, integration & test of space systems
Experience with launch and early orbit testing
Experience with prototypes and transitioning technology to operational systems

How You Can Stand Out

It would be impressive if you have one or more of these:

Demonstrated outstanding record keeping of risks, issues, watch list items for major programs
Demonstrated independent and outside the box thinking for risk mitigation
Ability to thrive in dynamic environment, and under sometimes nebulous or ambiguous guidelines

Battelle delivers when others can’t. We conduct research and development, manage national laboratories, design and manufacture products and deliver critical services for our clients—whether they are a multi-national corporation, a small start-up or a government agency.

We recognize and appreciate the value and contributions of individuals from a wide range of backgrounds and experiences and welcome all qualified individuals to apply.

Job Summary

The Environment and Agriculture (E&A) Business Line is part of the Environment and Infrastructure Business Unit in Battelle’s Applied Science & Technology Organization. E&A is responsible for delivering strategic growth and business priorities focused on a wide range of environmental and agriculture crop protection services.

The Environmental Solutions Division is responsible for developing and delivering environmental services for contaminated sites from assessments through remediation, natural resource management, environmental data management, and general environmental support. The Environmental Solutions Division Manager will have operational responsibility for approximately 100 staff and over $50 million in revenue from Government and Commercial clients. The Environmental Solutions Division Manager is responsible for the implementation of the environmental portion of the E&A annual growth and business plan, including managing relationships with clients and other stakeholders. Specific responsibilities include.

This position is located in Columbus, OH.

Responsibilities

Leads the Division to achieve growth year/year and profitable performance.
Develops and implements strategic and operational business plans that define the market focus and operational services the assigned group will provide to clients.
Responsible for the overall financial performance of the assigned group including attaining gross business volume, net income, and intellectual property goals as well as maximizing profitability, cost control, and investment decisions. Manages resource expenditures including percent time on project for staff, capital equipment, marketing, and internal research and development budgets.
Plans, initiates, and performs marketing activities to identify potential clients, new business segments, and market needs to maximize business opportunities. Contributes to proposals and bid/no bid decision processes. Establishes pricing policy and specific pricing practices.
Performs manpower planning and ensures appropriate staffing levels and skill mix commensurate with the business. Directs and organizes staff assignments for various projects.
Manages human resource activities such as developing recruiting strategy and hiring staff, establishing performance goals and appraising performance, and providing opportunities for career development. Manages relationships of staff and other groups.
Provides necessary training and mentor opportunities for staff.
Ensures staff conducts research, development, and technical activities within the established business ethics, safety, and quality
policies and procedures. Reviews and approves, as necessary, proposals, reports, and articles.
Directs efforts to produce efficient sales results and assures that sales investments are consistent with the Battelle strategic thrust areas.
Works across Battelle market sectors, global businesses, and national laboratories to ensure continuity and coordination in the areas of business development, client management, program management, and opportunity expansion. Plans effective teaming arrangements, establishes shared accountabilities and shared returns, and monitors results.
Manages facility and equipment needs including space requirements, new facility and modification decisions, and procurement for home office and offsite locations.
Develops and maintains relationships with key clients and federal agencies and their staff. Exhibits a clear understanding of customer requirements to ensure customer satisfaction.
Implements, executes, and communicates the policies and strategic emphasis of senior leadership to staff. Integrates decisions into operating policies.

Key Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in engineering, chemistry, environmental science, or a related field.
10 years of relevant line management experience.
Demonstrated experience in the environmental management field, with emphasis on site management and remediation.
Demonstrated experience with business development and client account management.
Must have sufficient communication skills to effectively interact with senior leadership and within client organizations, subcontractors, consultants, and staff. Requires critical human relation skills to understand, select, develop, and motivate others.
Broad-based experience communicating with clients and industry consortiums.
Must be a highly motivated self-starter.
Up to 50% travel expected for business development and client interactions.

Preferred Qualifications

A master’s degree or MBA is preferred.
Experience working with emerging contaminants is highly preferred.
Experience managing environmental operations across a broad range of services with demonstrated experience in project financial management, risk management, quality systems, and health and safety.

Benefits: Live an Extraordinary Life

We care about your well-being, not just on the job. Battelle offers comprehensive and competitive benefits to help you live your best life.

Balance life through a compressed work schedule: Most of our team follows a flexible, compressed work schedule that allows for every other Friday off—giving you a dedicated day to accomplish things in your personal life without using vacation time.
Enjoy enhanced work flexibility, including a hybrid arrangement: You have options for where and when you work. Our Together with Flexibility model allows you to work 60% in-office and 40% remote, with Monday and Tuesday as common in-office days, dependent on team and position needs.
Take time to recharge: You get paid time off to support work-life balance and keep motivated.
Prioritize wellness: Stay healthy with medical, dental, and vision coverage with wellness incentives and benefits plus a variety of optional supplemental benefits.
Better together: Coverage for partners, gender-affirming care and health support, and family formation support.
Build your financial future: Build financial stability with an industry-leading 401(k) retirement savings plan. For most employees, we put in 5 percent whether you contribute or not, and match your contributions on top of that.
Advance your education: Tuition assistance is available to pursue higher education.

A Work Environment Where You Succeed

For brilliant minds in science, technology, engineering and business operations, Battelle is the place to do the greatest good by solving humanity’s most pressing challenges and creating a safer, healthier and more secure world.

You will have the opportunity to thrive in a culture that inspires you to:

Apply your talent to challenging and meaningful projects
Receive select funding to pursue ideas in scientific and technological discovery
Partner with world-class experts in a collaborative environment

Manage environmental consultants and contractors as needed to support permitting, compliance, remediation, sustainability, and environmental improvement projects.

Demonstrated experience managing environmental permitting programs, regulatory reporting, and agency interactions.
Working knowledge of RCRA hazardous waste regulations, air permitting, water permitting, stormwater compliance, and environmental auditing practices.
Experience participating in or leading Management of Change (MOC) processes.

jobs.title: SCI Seasonal Restoration Technician
jobs.description:
Overview

SERG seeks two (2) Seasonal Restoration Technicians for habitat restoration, rare plant surveys, and other botany-related projects on San Clemente Island, a Naval installation on the southernmost of California’s Channel Islands. The Seasonal Restoration Technician position requires arduous manual labor, working outdoors in all weather, heavy lifting and carrying, and hiking on rugged terrain. This position will report to and work directly with the Crew Lead or Botany Project Manager, along with a crew of up to two other Seasonal Technicians and five other permanent staff members. The Seasonal Restoration Technician position will start on February 2, 2027, and end in May 2027. This is a full-time, hourly position. Compensation will be $23.31/hour plus a full benefits package. Housing is provided while working on San Clemente Island. The work schedule will be 10 days working on-island and 4-day weekends off-island. Housing is not provided during the 4-day weekends off-island. Transportation to and from the island is provided from the San Diego area by means of a twin engine 19-seater plane. Relocation benefits will not be offered.

All work will be conducted on San Clemente Island, which is owned and operated by the U.S. Navy as an active training site, as part of the Navy’s Natural Resources Program. San Clemente Island has a particularly unique flora, hosting 2 federally listed plants, 18 plants that are known from nowhere else in the world, and an additional 26 plants that are only known from islands off the coast of southern California or Baja. The program also supports an extensive community of biologists and researchers. Applicants should enjoy living as part of a small and remote community, and be able to maintain a professional, positive attitude at all times.

Responsibilities

The SCI Seasonal Restoration Technician is responsible for, but not limited to:

Field Work 80%

Monitor rare plant populations
Monitor vegetation cover
Maintain and monitor native species outplantings
Collect native plant propagules
Propagate native plants

Data Entry and Other Office Work 15%

Use GPS in the field and GIS software
Enter data and maintain databases

Other Duties and Responsibilities as assigned 5%

Ability to interact effectively with co-workers, contractors, and Navy personnel

Highly motivated individual with a high energy level and strong interpersonal skills.
Possess good judgment and common sense.

Experience with GIS

This position develops, operates, and maintains enterprise GIS data, applications, and workflows. The GIS Specialist independently scopes and delivers assigned GIS solutions; performs spatial and database analysis; develops and maintains GIS applications and datasets; tests and documents technical work; supports users; and collaborates with internal staff, and partners. Work is performed using organizational standards and may include water, electric, infrastructure, field mobility, asset management, and other enterprise GIS applications.

Pay

To have your application considered for the first round of interviews, please apply by Wednesday, October 7th, 2026, at 11:59 PM CST.

Applications will be accepted until the position is filled.

The City of Rochester will not sponsor or transfer visas for this position including F1 OPT STEM.

Duties And Responsibilities

The work below is representative of the scope of work performed within this job classification. Individual job duties will vary based on work assignment . Support GIS administration and related technology.

Support GIS plans , systems, and solutions to meet Department needs .
Operate and maintain the enterprise GIS.
Assist in the development and administration of the departmental GIS work plan.
Independently scope, develop, test, document, and deliver assigned GIS applications, workflows, data products, and technical solutions.
Collaborate with customers, departments, and outside agencies to integrate GIS solutions with related systems and business processes.

Develop, maintain, and administer Department GIS data and databases.

Create and update public and associated private infrastructure GIS datasets?

Test data processes and database changes; document results and coordinate implementation according to established change-management practices.
Provide public service to consultants, developers, citizens, and other agencies.
Work with other departments and governmental offices in developing and maintaining GIS databases for multiple users.
Respond to inquiries and requests for information about Department infrastructure.
Coordinate with other governmental GIS groups.
Prepare technical information for Boards, Councils, City staff agencies, Commissions, neighborhood groups, and professional organizations.
Provide training, guidance and technical support and provide guidance to department and division personnel on GIS, cartographic design, or other mapping requirements.

jobs.title: WA Conservation Transactions Director
jobs.description:
What We Can Achieve Together

The Washington Conservation Transactions Director manages the Conservation Transactions Team in planning, coordinating and implementing real estate and other conservation transactions for The Nature Conservancy’s Washington Business Unit and supporting transactions within the Western U.S. and Canada Division. They use the full range of protection tools (gift, easement, purchase, lease registry, conservation brokerage and cooperative projects) with public and private partners as appropriate to build and maintain conservation area systems that are: (1) ecologically representative and climate resilient, (2) effectively managed to deliver conservation outcomes, (3) durable because of sustainable finance, policies, and the commitment of stakeholders/rightsholders, and (4) inclusive in providing voice, authority and benefit to Indigenous Peoples and local communities.

We’re Looking For You

The Nature Conservancy is working toward a future where all people benefit equally from clean air and water, and our most critical lands and waters are connected, protected, and managed to sustain nature and communities in the face of climate change. As WA Conservation Transactions Director, you are responsible for leading a key functional team while engaging collaboratively and cooperatively with a broad range of staff and leaders to collectively advance conservation priorities in Washington state and beyond. You will drive alignment of conservation transaction efforts towards organizational priorities and provide real estate and transactions expertise to resolve legal, neighbor or community concerns associated with our land portfolio. You will represent the organization on transactions with external audiences, building authentic relationships with partners and serve on project teams to plan, negotiate, and implement transactions. new_jobs.description:
Overview

Be part of the solution - shape the future of our water environment.

Do you have the drive, skills and career potential to work with us as an experienced invasive species scientist, influencing environmental outcomes for our freshwater systems at the project level and beyond? We are seeking to further expand our team of freshwater ecologists within AtkinsRéalis' Water Management Consultancy. If you are looking to join an established team focused on the delivery of interesting and significant projects, framed by a strong culture of wellbeing, innovation and inclusivity, this is the place for you.

Our Water Management Consultancy operates at the interface between people and the water environment. Our key services cover all aspects of water management including aquatic ecology, hydromorphology, river restoration, flood and coastal erosion risk management, integrated catchment management, regulation and assurance, strategic asset management, water resources and water quality planning, hydrogeology and hydrology, climate futures and resilience, coastal and marine environmental management, natural capital and Biodiversity Net Gain assessment and economic appraisal. We have a reputation for technical excellence, innovation and actively shaping the future of our industry. We are a friendly and approachable team. We enjoy the work we do and have fun while doing it.

We have a huge variety of projects on-the-go at any one time. So, when you start this role with us, it could take your career wherever your interests lie. You'll find everyone here is willing to pitch in and help because we all want you to succeed, and we're ready to help you grow.

When it comes to living your life, we want you to get the most out of it. So, talk to us about all our flexible and remote working policies that can support your personal priorities. Also, ask us about some of our recent pledges for Women's'Equality, as well as being a 'Disability Confident' and 'Inclusive Employer.'"

AtkinsRéalis is one of the world's most respected design, engineering and project management consultancies. Our global team of over 38,000 employees speaks over 70 languages and represents 130 nationalities across six continents. At AtkinsRéalis, we offer more than just a job. We offer an opportunity to make a difference and shape the world to benefit future generations and the natural environment.

We understand the need for a diverse and flexible workforce, where a work-life balance is important. So, by default AtkinsRéalis offers flexible working, where there is no fixed 9 'till 5, no need for a 5-day week, no requirement for a full-time contract, and no requirement to spend all your working time in the office. Our IT systems support homeworking, so where you have parental or carer duties; or you simply need to be elsewhere for a parcel, servicing your car, or waiting in for a tradesperson; AtkinsRéalis will work for you. Similarly, AtkinsRéalis' corporate social responsibility provides the opportunity to give something back to the community, and we run professional networks supporting groups such as local schools, charities, parents, those coming out of the armed-forces and women in engineering.

As an experienced aquatic ecologist with a focus on assessing and managing the impacts of invasive non-native species (INNS) on the freshwater environment, you can expect to support the delivery of work within our INNS Service Line team. Your work will produce tangible improvements within river catchments throughout the UK support by the dynamic and influential relationship between our aquatic ecology team, water resource specialists and our engineering design and planning colleagues. Our structure and growing project portfolio will provide exceptional opportunities for you to develop your career.

You should have a strong technical background in aquatic INNS investigation and management, that includes application of industry standard risk assessment tools (e.g., SAI-RAT) for water resource transfers, the development and management of INNS monitoring programmes and analysis of ecological monitoring data. You should exhibit strong collaborative behaviours to interface with other technical specialists.

You will also have the chance to develop yourself though wider opportunities and support on our increasing portfolio of UK water resource investigations, infrastructure planning and development support, and habitat management and design projects. We work for clients across the UK and overseas, including water companies, central government, regulators, NGOs and local authorities.

This Position is open for Birmingham, Bristol, Derby, Epsom, Glasgow, Edinburgh, Manchester, Oxford or Peterborough Offices.

Your role

To support water resource INNS investigations and develop the application of risk assessment tools for our key water company and regulatory clients.
To support our INNS Service Line team with work activities through integration and collaboration with multi-disciplinary teams and bring your technical knowledge and influence to bear in securing the best outcomes for the environment and our clients.
To support the development and application of emerging approaches in INNS management, transfer and control to ensure the technical development of staff within our aquatic ecology team.

The Washington Conservation Transactions Director manages the Conservation Transactions Team in planning, coordinating and implementing real estate and other conservation transactions for The Nature Conservancy’s Washington Business Unit and supporting transactions within the Western U.S. and Canada Division. They use the full range of protection tools (gift, easement, purchase, lease registry, conservation brokerage and cooperative projects) with public and private partners as appropriate to build and maintain conservation area systems that are: (1) ecologically representative and climate resilient, (2) effectively managed to deliver conservation outcomes, (3) durable because of sustainable finance, policies, and the commitment of stakeholders/rightsholders, and (4) inclusive in providing voice, authority and benefit to Indigenous Peoples and local communities.

We’re Looking For You

The Nature Conservancy is working toward a future where all people benefit equally from clean air and water, and our most critical lands and waters are connected, protected, and managed to sustain nature and communities in the face of climate change. As WA Conservation Transactions Director, you are responsible for leading a key functional team while engaging collaboratively and cooperatively with a broad range of staff and leaders to collectively advance conservation priorities in Washington state and beyond. You will drive alignment of conservation transaction efforts towards organizational priorities and provide real estate and transactions expertise to resolve legal, neighbor or community concerns associated with our land portfolio. You will represent the organization on transactions with external audiences, building authentic relationships with partners and serve on project teams to plan, negotiate, and implement transactions. We seek a candidate who embodies a strong spirit of collaboration and relationship building, possesses adept project management skills, and demonstrates creative problem-solving abilities, all while bringing a methodical and comprehensive approach to spearheading our conservation transactions. Through this work, you’ll play a significant role in TNC’s ambitious goals for a better future for people and nature.

This role requires a cover letter. Applicants may use this opportunity to describe their interest in the position, relevant leadership experience, and how their background aligns with the responsibilities and goals of the role.

Essential Functions Include

Manage and Execute Conservation Transactions (50%)

Design, coordinate, and execute complex and innovative conservation transactions across all program areas to conserve and steward lands for increased climate resiliency and biodiversity.
Serve as the principal project manager and/or lead negotiator on complex transactions with government agencies, other conservation organizations, Tribes, and private individuals and entities.
Support/advise conservation staff and partners on the application and adaptation of transactional tools for advancing conservation outcomes.
Work closely with conservation, legal, finance, government relations, marketing, philanthropy, and science teams in deployment of the full range of protection approaches the Conservancy uses, including policy initiatives, community-led conservation, land protection transactions and preserve transfers.
Assist in securing public and private funds for land protection by supporting TNC's fundraising efforts, participating in donor engagements, meetings, and proposals, and by preparing public grant proposals and reports.
Research land ownership information for tracts identified as potential acquisition projects, respond to protection inquiries, screen potential projects, and prepare and steward project approval packages through internal approval processes, as appropriate.
Support efforts to adjust our portfolio of lands assets (conservation easements, preserves, and other lands TNC manages) by working with organizational leadership to approve real estate projects and complete transactions.

Relationship Building and External Collaboration (25%)

Represent the Conservancy in relationships and negotiations with stakeholders/ rightsholders, working collaboratively to improve decisions, transparency, and strengthen bilateral commitments.
Build and sustain relationships with conservation partners including Tribes to implement and achieve the Conservancy’s conservation priorities.
Partner with Community Relations Managers to engage local community support for conservation efforts.

Team Management (25%)

Manage a team of 2-3 professional staff and team budget, ensuring clear performance expectations and alignment with organizational priorities.
Manage overall workflow of the transactions team to ensure effective coordination and support for priority work, while ensuring sustainable workloads for team members.
Build a team culture of innovation, learning, collaboration, risk management, and accountability that is centered on integrity and an equitable approach to transactions.

Responsibilites and Scope

Level of Position: The WA Conservation Transactions Director is a senior conservation manager within the Washington Business Unit. They develop strategic direction, have significant financial responsibility and discretion over functional team level budget decisions, and are accountable for conservation results within their control. Geographic size and scope is that of a complex business unit or multiple business units.

Within the scope of this position, the WA Conservation Transactions Director will:

Supervise professional and administrative staff working toward accomplishment of program goals with responsibility for performance management, training and career development.
Negotiate real estate transactions, which can bind the Conservancy legally and financially.
Plan and direct work on protection projects.
Be responsible for timely resolution of conservation real estate legal matters to protect conservation values, maintain good standing as a neighbor, and minimize risks to the organization.
Regularly coordinate with other Business Unit Protection teams in the Western U.S. and Canada Division to meet, plan, and identify priority and/or regional projects for collaborative implementation to further Divisional priorities.
Adaptively manage TNC’s transactions project pipeline in coordination with other Washington or Divisional teams to assess and prioritize new acquisitions that further conservation goals, preserve transfers, and land assists.
Collaborate with land transaction practitioners in the Western U.S. and Canada Division and across the North America Region to share resources and lessons learned.
Partner with philanthropy, public funding, marketing and other functional staff to support fundraising efforts for transaction projects.
Resolve complex problems independently with minimal supervision.
